BackDown 1.0.0-beta.5

The fifth beta of BackDown 1.0: the swarm (every machine you run BackDown on as one, with a shared pool to file drives into), people and databases gathered across drives, search inside mail and databases that reuses the indexes already there, files fetched from whichever machine holds them, a phone .

Released 2026-11-02 · downloads and checksums on GitHub · Download page The fifth beta of BackDown 1.0: the swarm (every machine you run BackDown on as one, with a shared pool to file drives into), people and databases gathered across drives, search inside mail and databases that reuses the indexes already there, files fetched from whichever machine holds them, a phone app, and a long list of fixes and tidying.

Install#

PlatformInstallerCommand line
Linux x86-64backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.5_amd64.deb (Debian, Ubuntu) or .AppImagebackdown-v1.0.0-beta.5-linux-x86_64.tar.gz (static)
Linux ARM64backdown-io_1.0.0-beta.5_arm64.deb or .AppImagebackdown-v1.0.0-beta.5-linux-arm64.tar.gz (static)
macOS (Apple silicon + Intel)BackDown-1.0.0-beta.5.dmgbackdown-v1.0.0-beta.5-macos-universal.tar.gz
Windows x86-64BackDown-1.0.0-beta.5-x64.msi (no administrator rights needed)backdown-v1.0.0-beta.5-windows-x86_64.zip

This release is signed. SHA256SUMS.txt.sig is an Ed25519 signature of SHA256SUMS.txt by BackDown's release key, and backdown update checks it before installing anything. To check by hand, see Air-gapped computers.

The installers and apps themselves still aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft. On macOS, right-click the app and choose Open the first time (for the command-line binary: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine backdown). On Windows, SmartScreen may ask you to confirm once.

What's new since beta.4#

The swarm, and the pool#

  • Every machine as one. The machines backdown remote reaches, plus this one, show up together: each machine's drives as bars of used and free space, what's indexed on them, their health, drives that aren't connected and the machine they were last scanned on, and the totals. backdown swarm, and the browser's Swarm view. A drive is known by its serial and volume UUID, so one that moves between machines is the same drive.
  • Where is it. backdown swarm where NAME and the Swarm view's search ask every machine at once, live where it can be reached and from what was synced where it can't: machine, drive, path.
  • The pool. backdown pool add FOLDER [--reserve 50G] [--takes Mail,Media] makes a folder on one of a machine's drives part of a shared, filed archive; the other machines learn of it at their next sync. The pool keeps one copy of each file.
  • A drive into the pool. backdown pool plan DRIVE says, thing by thing, what's in the pool already (by SHA-256, on any machine), what's new, and which pool folder each thing goes into and why; you move or leave out what you like; backdown pool send copies it, verified by the hash read back there, resumable, and then offers to free the drive. It works for a drive plugged into another machine too, from here: the plan is made and carried out there, by that machine's own BackDown. Copies between machines stream over ssh to backdown swarm-stdio, which writes only inside that machine's own pool folders.
  • Several machines is free now, as the swarm is built on it.
  • Syncing a big drive from another machine no longer times out; what to ask it to read is found in seconds rather than a minute a batch.

Files from whichever machine holds them#

  • A file on another machine's page has Preview, Download a copy and Open, and backdown remote fetch nas PATH -o DIR saves one here from the terminal, checked against the hash that machine has. The other machine reads a file only if it's still exactly as its index scanned it. Files up to 256 MB come through a small cache here so a second look costs nothing; bigger ones stream the part asked for. Indexing stays each machine's own business: this brings one file you asked for, never a drive.

People and databases#

  • More kinds of thing recognised: mongodump folders, SQLite files, and the data directories of MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL and MongoDB servers; dump headers from phpMyAdmin, pg_dump, pg_dumpall and SQLite's .dump; and what a website's or Nextcloud server's configuration says (wp-config.php, Joomla, Laravel .env, Nextcloud config.php): the database behind it, where it was served, who to contact.
  • People (backdown people, What's here > People): everyone with a mailbox in a mail store, a Nextcloud account, a home folder, a Thunderbird identity or named as a site's contact, gathered across drives into one person with what there is of them. The same address, or the same login on the same host, is one person; a name alone never merges two.
  • Databases (backdown databases, What's here > Databases): each database with every dump of it, its live data, its SQLite file, and the sites and servers configured to use it, under one name per engine family.

Search inside mail and databases#

  • backdown search WORDS and the search box's Inside scope find messages by subject, sender and recipient, and dumps and SQLite files by table, column and (at full depth) the text in their rows.
  • Indexes already on the drives are reused: Dovecot's own dovecot.index.cache is read for the headers of a whole mailbox without opening a message; SQLite full-text tables (FTS3/4/5) are searched in place through SQLite itself; a dump's FULLTEXT KEY columns are listed with the table.
  • Depth is a setting (off, headers, full); the service indexes after each recognition, only drives scanned since. The index keeps no copy of the text, only where each hit is.

The app and the browser#

  • BackDown for Android and iOS (Flutter): the browser's views on a phone, over the same connection. backdown token --qr shows the link for other devices as a QR code.
  • Remove a drive from the index, from its page or backdown forget, scans and all; and a scan in progress can be stopped.
  • Settings has real tabs, one section at a time.
  • backdown open, token and app say whose daemon is on the port instead of "none is running".
  • The Machines page keeps each drive's cached and hashed counts across syncs.
  • A live UI preview for development (scripts/preview-ui.py).

The store#

  • Pro, Team and Forensic pre-orders, each with its own licence; licences name their edition and count Forensic seats as sites. Nothing is switched on in this release: everything stays unlocked during the beta.

Fixes and under the hood#

  • Hashing: a file no longer inherits another file's SHA-256 through a reused inode number.
  • The spreadsheet viewer moved off a zip release with a known vulnerability (zip 9, calamine 0.37).
  • One transaction type that rolls back when dropped, so a failed job can't leave one open; one clock, one hex decoder, one mount-table reader, one mbox rule instead of several copies.
  • The viewers (archives, disk images, mail, spreadsheets, slides, SQL dumps) are a crate of their own, and the recogniser, rescue carving, update, mailbox and mail-merge modules are split into files by stage.
  • The pre-Rust scripts moved to legacy/, with a README.

Known limitations#

  • Built locally, not by CI. Every test passed on Linux; the macOS and Windows builds are checked but haven't yet run on those systems. Please report anything that doesn't work: https://github.com/BuenGenio/backdown-releases/issues
  • The installers aren't signed or notarised by Apple or Microsoft.
  • Pro, Team and Forensic features are free during the beta; pricing may change before 1.0.
  • Reading Dovecot's own index cache has been checked against Dovecot's file format and a synthetic cache, not yet against a large real server's; anything odd falls back to reading the messages.
  • A machine running Windows can't be the other end of backdown remote yet.

Documentation: https://backdown.io/docs/. Provided as-is, without warranty, for evaluation.
